technologies: The inspected adapter selects rigorloop-records-v3, whose manifest and supporting records declare schema version 3. SHA-256 byte identities and synchronous Node filesystem calls support the storage protocol. This operational JSON format is independent of the new design/ authoring schemas.

sources.locator: packages/rigorloop/dist/lib/record-store.js Store, executeTargetedStore, executeRecordStore, withRecordSnapshot; record-store-files.js RecordFiles; remaining software_units at 9055b3c0
sources.basis: Static inspection identifies transaction mechanisms, format dispatch, construction, and physical co-location; it does not execute fault, durability, preservation, or recovery verification.

proposed.choice: Retain registered filesystem JSON records and exact before/candidate journaling for the current operational contract.
proposed.rationale: SR-042 through SR-045 require compatible records, byte preservation, fresh publication, and exact explicit recovery; the existing store provides a concrete design basis.
alternatives: A transactional database could provide a different transaction boundary, but would require an explicit record, identity, recovery, and historical migration design.
consequences: Keep the retained external-editor and filesystem support limits. Multiple-file coherence is a store protocol, not an assertion that one filesystem rename publishes the entire record set.
revisit_when: Measured workload, remote concurrency, or platform limitations make the current protocol inadequate and a compatible migration can be specified.
